Mathematical definitions of the test problems

Source: vignettes/articles/problem-definitions.Rmd
problem-definitions.Rmd

Use this page to find the residual equations, supported dimensions, and standard starting point for any problem implemented by funconstrain. The definitions follow Section 3 of Moré, Garbow, and Hillstrom (1981) using one notation throughout. The authors’ Algorithm 566 source is a second primary source for resolving typographical and indexing ambiguities.

The formulas follow those sources; the dimensions and defaults describe the current package. Where funconstrain supports a narrower range, that range is shown. To run a problem, see Getting started with funconstrain or the funconstrain_problem() reference.

For x=(x1,…,xn)∈ℝnx=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n, every problem below defines mm residuals. The scalar callback returned by the package is

F(x)=∑i=1mri(x)2,𝚙𝚛𝚘𝚋𝚕𝚎𝚖$𝚏𝚗(𝚡)=F(x). F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}r_i(x)^2, \qquad \texttt{problem\$fn(x)}=F(x).

Indices in the equations are one-based. A sum over an empty index range is zero. x(0)x^{(0)} denotes the standard starting point.

1. Rosenbrock Function

Dimensions: n=2n=2, m=2m=2
Factory: rosen()

r1(x)=10(x2−x12),r2(x)=1−x1. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10(x_2-x_1^2),\\ r_2(x)&=1-x_1. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(−1.2,1)x^{(0)}=(-1.2,1)

2. Freudenstein and Roth Function

Dimensions: n=2n=2, m=2m=2
Factory: freud_roth()

r1(x)=−13+x1+{(5−x2)x2−2}x2,r2(x)=−29+x1+{(1+x2)x2−14}x2. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=-13+x_1+\{(5-x_2)x_2-2\}x_2,\\ r_2(x)&=-29+x_1+\{(1+x_2)x_2-14\}x_2. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(1/2,−2)x^{(0)}=(1/2,-2)

3. Powell Badly Scaled Function

Dimensions: n=2n=2, m=2m=2
Factory: powell_bs()

r1(x)=104x1x2−1,r2(x)=e−x1+e−x2−1.0001. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10^4x_1x_2-1,\\ r_2(x)&=e^{-x_1}+e^{-x_2}-1.0001. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(0,1)x^{(0)}=(0,1)

4. Brown Badly Scaled Function

Dimensions: n=2n=2, m=3m=3
Factory: brown_bs()

r1(x)=x1−106,r2(x)=x2−2×10−6,r3(x)=x1x2−2. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=x_1-10^6,\\ r_2(x)&=x_2-2\times10^{-6},\\ r_3(x)&=x_1x_2-2. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(1,1)x^{(0)}=(1,1)

5. Beale Function

Dimensions: n=2n=2, m=3m=3
Factory: beale()

For i=1,2,3i=1,2,3, let (c1,c2,c3)=(1.5,2.25,2.625)(c_1,c_2,c_3)=(1.5,2.25,2.625). Then

ri(x)=ci−x1(1−x2i). r_i(x)=c_i-x_1(1-x_2^i).

Start: x(0)=(1,1)x^{(0)}=(1,1)

6. Jennrich and Sampson Function

Dimensions: n=2n=2, m≥2m\ge2; default m=10m=10
Factory: jenn_samp()

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m,

ri(x)=2+2i−eix1−eix2. r_i(x)=2+2i-e^{ix_1}-e^{ix_2}.

Start: x(0)=(0.3,0.4)x^{(0)}=(0.3,0.4)

7. Helical Valley Function

Dimensions: n=3n=3, m=3m=3
Factory: helical()

Away from (x1,x2)=(0,0)(x_1,x_2)=(0,0), define

θ(x1,x2)={12πtan⁡−1(x2/x1),x1>0,12πtan⁡−1(x2/x1)+12,x1<0,14sgn⁡(x2),x1=0. \theta(x_1,x_2)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\tan^{-1}(x_2/x_1),&x_1>0,\\[4pt] \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\tan^{-1}(x_2/x_1)+\dfrac12,&x_1<0,\\[4pt] \dfrac14\operatorname{sgn}(x_2),&x_1=0. \end{cases}

The residuals are

r1(x)=10{x3−10θ(x1,x2)},r2(x)=10{(x12+x22)1/2−1},r3(x)=x3. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10\{x_3-10\theta(x_1,x_2)\},\\ r_2(x)&=10\{(x_1^2+x_2^2)^{1/2}-1\},\\ r_3(x)&=x_3. \end{aligned}

Implementation note: The package rejects the origin, where the objective is undefined.

Start: x(0)=(−1,0,0)x^{(0)}=(-1,0,0)

8. Bard Function

Dimensions: n=3n=3, m=15m=15
Factory: bard()

For i=1,…,15i=1,\ldots,15, set vi=16−iv_i=16-i, wi=min⁡(i,vi)w_i=\min(i,v_i), and

(y1,…,y15)=(0.14,0.18,0.22,0.25,0.29,0.32,0.35,0.39,0.37,0.58,0.73,0.96,1.34,2.10,4.39). \begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{15})={}&(0.14,0.18,0.22,0.25,0.29,0.32,0.35,0.39,\\ &0.37,0.58,0.73,0.96,1.34,2.10,4.39). \end{aligned}

Then

ri(x)=yi−(x1+ivix2+wix3). r_i(x)=y_i-\left(x_1+\frac{i}{v_ix_2+w_ix_3}\right).

Start: x(0)=(1,1,1)x^{(0)}=(1,1,1)

9. Gaussian Function

Dimensions: n=3n=3, m=15m=15
Factory: gauss()

For i=1,…,15i=1,\ldots,15, set ti=(8−i)/2t_i=(8-i)/2 and

(y1,…,y15)=(0.0009,0.0044,0.0175,0.0540,0.1295,0.2420,0.3521,0.3989,0.3521,0.2420,0.1295,0.0540,0.0175,0.0044,0.0009). \begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{15})={}&(0.0009,0.0044,0.0175,0.0540,0.1295,\\ &0.2420,0.3521,0.3989,0.3521,0.2420,\\ &0.1295,0.0540,0.0175,0.0044,0.0009). \end{aligned}

Then

ri(x)=x1exp⁡{−x22(ti−x3)2}−yi. r_i(x)=x_1\exp\left\{-\frac{x_2}{2}(t_i-x_3)^2\right\}-y_i.

Start: x(0)=(0.4,1,0)x^{(0)}=(0.4,1,0)

10. Meyer Function

Dimensions: n=3n=3, m=16m=16
Factory: meyer()

For i=1,…,16i=1,\ldots,16, set ti=45+5it_i=45+5i and

(y1,…,y16)=(34780,28610,23650,19630,16370,13720,11540,9744,8261,7030,6005,5147,4427,3820,3307,2872). \begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{16})={}&(34780,28610,23650,19630,16370,13720,11540,9744,\\ &8261,7030,6005,5147,4427,3820,3307,2872). \end{aligned}

Then

ri(x)=x1exp⁡(x2ti+x3)−yi. r_i(x)=x_1\exp\left(\frac{x_2}{t_i+x_3}\right)-y_i.

Start: x(0)=(0.02,4000,250)x^{(0)}=(0.02,4000,250)

11. Gulf Research and Development Function

Dimensions: n=3n=3, 3≤m≤1003\le m\le100; default m=99m=99
Factory: gulf()

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m, define

ti=i100,yi=25+{−50log⁡(ti)}2/3. t_i=\frac{i}{100},\qquad y_i=25+\{-50\log(t_i)\}^{2/3}.

The residual is

ri(x)=exp⁡{−|x2−yi|x3x1}−ti. r_i(x)=\exp\left\{-\frac{|x_2-y_i|^{x_3}}{x_1}\right\}-t_i.

Source note: The published equation has a typographical glyph where the subtraction in |x2−yi||x_2-y_i| should appear; the corrected form above agrees with the authors’ Algorithm 566 source and the package.

Start: x(0)=(5,2.5,0.15)x^{(0)}=(5,2.5,0.15)

12. Box Three-Dimensional Function

Dimensions: n=3n=3, m≥3m\ge3; default m=20m=20
Factory: box_3d()

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m, let ti=i/10t_i=i/10. Then

ri(x)=e−tix1−e−tix2−x3(e−ti−e−i). r_i(x)=e^{-t_ix_1}-e^{-t_ix_2}-x_3(e^{-t_i}-e^{-i}).

Start: x(0)=(0,10,20)x^{(0)}=(0,10,20)

13. Powell Singular Function

Dimensions: n=4n=4, m=4m=4
Factory: powell_s()

r1(x)=x1+10x2,r2(x)=5(x3−x4),r3(x)=(x2−2x3)2,r4(x)=10(x1−x4)2. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=x_1+10x_2,\\ r_2(x)&=\sqrt5(x_3-x_4),\\ r_3(x)&=(x_2-2x_3)^2,\\ r_4(x)&=\sqrt{10}(x_1-x_4)^2. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(3,−1,0,1)x^{(0)}=(3,-1,0,1)

14. Wood Function

Dimensions: n=4n=4, m=6m=6
Factory: wood()

r1(x)=10(x2−x12),r2(x)=1−x1,r3(x)=90(x4−x32),r4(x)=1−x3,r5(x)=10(x2+x4−2),r6(x)=(x2−x4)/10. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=10(x_2-x_1^2),&r_2(x)&=1-x_1,\\ r_3(x)&=\sqrt{90}(x_4-x_3^2),&r_4(x)&=1-x_3,\\ r_5(x)&=\sqrt{10}(x_2+x_4-2),& r_6(x)&=(x_2-x_4)/\sqrt{10}. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(−3,−1,−3,−1)x^{(0)}=(-3,-1,-3,-1)

15. Kowalik and Osborne Function

Dimensions: n=4n=4, m=11m=11
Factory: kow_osb()

The data are

(y1,…,y11)=(0.1957,0.1947,0.1735,0.1600,0.0844,0.0627,0.0456,0.0342,0.0323,0.0235,0.0246),(u1,…,u11)=(4,2,1,0.5,0.25,0.167,0.125,0.1,0.0833,0.0714,0.0625). \begin{aligned} (y_1,\ldots,y_{11})={}&(0.1957,0.1947,0.1735,0.1600,0.0844,0.0627,\\ &0.0456,0.0342,0.0323,0.0235,0.0246),\\ (u_1,\ldots,u_{11})={}&(4,2,1,0.5,0.25,0.167,0.125,0.1,\\ &0.0833,0.0714,0.0625). \end{aligned}

For i=1,…,11i=1,\ldots,11,

ri(x)=yi−x1ui(ui+x2)ui(ui+x3)+x4. r_i(x)=y_i-x_1\frac{u_i(u_i+x_2)}{u_i(u_i+x_3)+x_4}.

16. Brown and Dennis Function

Dimensions: n=4n=4, m≥4m\ge4; default m=20m=20
Factory: brown_den()

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m, let ti=i/5t_i=i/5 and define

ai(x)=x1+tix2−eti,bi(x)=x3+x4sin⁡(ti)−cos⁡(ti),ri(x)=ai(x)2+bi(x)2. \begin{aligned} a_i(x)&=x_1+t_ix_2-e^{t_i},\\ b_i(x)&=x_3+x_4\sin(t_i)-\cos(t_i),\\ r_i(x)&=a_i(x)^2+b_i(x)^2. \end{aligned}

Objective note: This problem squares ai2+bi2a_i^2+b_i^2 once more in the shared objective F(x)=∑iri(x)2F(x)=\sum_i r_i(x)^2.

Start: x(0)=(25,5,−5,1)x^{(0)}=(25,5,-5,1)

For i=1,…,33i=1,\ldots,33,

18. Biggs EXP6 Function

Dimensions: n=6n=6, m≥6m\ge6; default m=13m=13
Factory: biggs_exp6()

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m, let ti=i/10t_i=i/10 and

yi=e−ti−5e−10ti+3e−4ti. y_i=e^{-t_i}-5e^{-10t_i}+3e^{-4t_i}.

Then

ri(x)=x3e−tix1−x4e−tix2+x6e−tix5−yi. r_i(x)=x_3e^{-t_ix_1}-x_4e^{-t_ix_2}+x_6e^{-t_ix_5}-y_i.

Start: x(0)=(1,2,1,1,1,1)x^{(0)}=(1,2,1,1,1,1)

20. Watson Function

Dimensions: 2≤n≤312\le n\le31, m=31m=31; default n=6n=6
Factory: watson()

For i=1,…,29i=1,\ldots,29, define

ti=i/29,ai(x)=∑j=2n(j−1)xjtij−2,bi(x)=∑j=1nxjtij−1. \begin{aligned} t_i&=i/29,\\ a_i(x)&=\sum_{j=2}^{n}(j-1)x_jt_i^{j-2},\\ b_i(x)&=\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_jt_i^{j-1}. \end{aligned}

The residuals are

ri(x)=ai(x)−bi(x)2−1,i=1,…,29,r30(x)=x1,r31(x)=x2−x12−1. \begin{aligned} r_i(x)&=a_i(x)-b_i(x)^2-1,&&i=1,\ldots,29,\\ r_{30}(x)&=x_1,\\ r_{31}(x)&=x_2-x_1^2-1. \end{aligned}

Start: x(0)=(0,…,0)x^{(0)}=(0,\ldots,0)

21. Extended Rosenbrock Function

Dimensions: even n≥2n\ge2, m=nm=n; default n=8n=8
Factory: ex_rosen()

For k=1,…,n/2k=1,\ldots,n/2,

r2k−1(x)=10(x2k−x2k−12),r2k(x)=1−x2k−1. \begin{aligned} r_{2k-1}(x)&=10(x_{2k}-x_{2k-1}^2),\\ r_{2k}(x)&=1-x_{2k-1}. \end{aligned}

Start: Repeat (−1.2,1)(-1.2,1) exactly n/2n/2 times.

22. Extended Powell Function

Dimensions: n≥4n\ge4 and divisible by 4, m=nm=n; default n=20n=20
Factory: ex_powell()

For k=1,…,n/4k=1,\ldots,n/4, let a=4k−3a=4k-3. Then

ra(x)=xa+10xa+1,ra+1(x)=5(xa+2−xa+3),ra+2(x)=(xa+1−2xa+2)2,ra+3(x)=10(xa−xa+3)2. \begin{aligned} r_a(x)&=x_a+10x_{a+1},\\ r_{a+1}(x)&=\sqrt5(x_{a+2}-x_{a+3}),\\ r_{a+2}(x)&=(x_{a+1}-2x_{a+2})^2,\\ r_{a+3}(x)&=\sqrt{10}(x_a-x_{a+3})^2. \end{aligned}

Naming note: MGH calls this the “Extended Powell singular” problem; the package title is shortened.

Start: Repeat (3,−1,0,1)(3,-1,0,1) exactly n/4n/4 times.

23. Penalty Function I

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=n+1m=n+1; default n=25n=25
Factory: penalty_1()

With a=10−5a=10^{-5},

rj(x)=a(xj−1),j=1,…,n,rn+1(x)=∑j=1nxj2−14. \begin{aligned} r_j(x)&=\sqrt{a}(x_j-1),&&j=1,\ldots,n,\\ r_{n+1}(x)&=\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j^2-\frac14. \end{aligned}

Start: xj(0)=jx_j^{(0)}=j

24. Penalty Function II

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=2nm=2n; default n=25n=25
Factory: penalty_2()

With a=10−5a=10^{-5}, the residuals are

r1(x)=x1−0.2,ri(x)=a{exi/10+exi−1/10−ei/10−e(i−1)/10},i=2,…,n,rn+i−1(x)=a{exi/10−e−0.1},i=2,…,n,r2n(x)=∑j=1n(n−j+1)xj2−1. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=x_1-0.2,\\ r_i(x)&=\sqrt a\{e^{x_i/10}+e^{x_{i-1}/10}-e^{i/10}-e^{(i-1)/10}\}, &&i=2,\ldots,n,\\ r_{n+i-1}(x)&=\sqrt a\{e^{x_i/10}-e^{-0.1}\}, &&i=2,\ldots,n,\\ r_{2n}(x)&=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(n-j+1)x_j^2-1. \end{aligned}

Edge case: For n=1n=1, the two middle ranges are empty.

Start: xj(0)=1/2x_j^{(0)}=1/2

25. Variably Dimensioned Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=n+2m=n+2; default n=30n=30
Factory: var_dim()

Define s(x)=∑j=1nj(xj−1)s(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}j(x_j-1). Then

rj(x)=xj−1,j=1,…,n,rn+1(x)=s(x),rn+2(x)=s(x)2. \begin{aligned} r_j(x)&=x_j-1,&&j=1,\ldots,n,\\ r_{n+1}(x)&=s(x),\\ r_{n+2}(x)&=s(x)^2. \end{aligned}

Start: xj(0)=1−j/nx_j^{(0)}=1-j/n

26. Trigonometric Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=nm=n; default n=30n=30
Factory: trigon()

For i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n,

ri(x)=n−∑j=1ncos⁡(xj)+i{1−cos⁡(xi)}−sin⁡(xi). r_i(x)=n-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\cos(x_j)+i\{1-\cos(x_i)\}-\sin(x_i).

Start: xj(0)=1/nx_j^{(0)}=1/n

27. Brown Almost-Linear Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=nm=n; default n=30n=30
Factory: brown_al()

ri(x)=xi+∑j=1nxj−(n+1),i=1,…,n−1,rn(x)=∏j=1nxj−1. \begin{aligned} r_i(x)&=x_i+\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j-(n+1),&&i=1,\ldots,n-1,\\ r_n(x)&=\prod_{j=1}^{n}x_j-1. \end{aligned}

Edge case: For n=1n=1, the first range is empty.

Start: xj(0)=1/2x_j^{(0)}=1/2

28. Discrete Boundary Value Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=nm=n; default n=35n=35
Factory: disc_bv()

Let h=1/(n+1)h=1/(n+1), ti=iht_i=ih, and set the boundary values x0=xn+1=0x_0=x_{n+1}=0. For i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n,

ri(x)=2xi−xi−1−xi+1+h22(xi+ti+1)3. r_i(x)=2x_i-x_{i-1}-x_{i+1}+\frac{h^2}{2}(x_i+t_i+1)^3.

Start: xi(0)=ti(ti−1)x_i^{(0)}=t_i(t_i-1)

29. Discrete Integral Equation Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=nm=n; default n=35n=35
Factory: disc_ie()

Let h=1/(n+1)h=1/(n+1), ti=iht_i=ih, and qj(x)=(xj+tj+1)3q_j(x)=(x_j+t_j+1)^3. For i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n,

ri(x)=xi+h2{(1−ti)∑j=1itjqj(x)+ti∑j=i+1n(1−tj)qj(x)}. r_i(x)=x_i+\frac{h}{2}\left\{ (1-t_i)\sum_{j=1}^{i}t_jq_j(x) +t_i\sum_{j=i+1}^{n}(1-t_j)q_j(x) \right\}.

Start: xi(0)=ti(ti−1)x_i^{(0)}=t_i(t_i-1)

30. Broyden Tridiagonal Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=nm=n; default n=40n=40
Factory: broyden_tri()

Set x0=xn+1=0x_0=x_{n+1}=0. For i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n,

ri(x)=(3−2xi)xi−xi−1−2xi+1+1. r_i(x)=(3-2x_i)x_i-x_{i-1}-2x_{i+1}+1.

Start: x(0)=(−1,…,−1)x^{(0)}=(-1,\ldots,-1)

31. Broyden Banded Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m=nm=n; default n=40n=40
Factory: broyden_band()

For each i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n, define

Bi={j:max⁡(1,i−5)≤j≤min⁡(n,i+1),j≠i}. B_i=\{j:\max(1,i-5)\le j\le\min(n,i+1),\ j\ne i\}.

Then

ri(x)=xi(2+5xi2)+1−∑j∈Bixj(1+xj). r_i(x)=x_i(2+5x_i^2)+1-\sum_{j\in B_i}x_j(1+x_j).

Start: x(0)=(−1,…,−1)x^{(0)}=(-1,\ldots,-1)

32. Linear Function - Full Rank

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m≥nm\ge n; defaults n=45n=45, m=100m=100
Factory: linfun_fr()

Define c(x)=1+(2/m)∑j=1nxjc(x)=1+(2/m)\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j. Then

ri(x)={xi−c(x),i=1,…,n,−c(x),i=n+1,…,m. r_i(x)= \begin{cases} x_i-c(x),&i=1,\ldots,n,\\ -c(x),&i=n+1,\ldots,m. \end{cases}

Start: x(0)=(1,…,1)x^{(0)}=(1,\ldots,1)

33. Linear Function - Rank 1

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m≥nm\ge n; defaults n=45n=45, m=100m=100
Factory: linfun_r1()

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m,

ri(x)=i∑j=1njxj−1. r_i(x)=i\sum_{j=1}^{n}jx_j-1.

Start: x(0)=(1,…,1)x^{(0)}=(1,\ldots,1)

34. Linear Function - Rank 1 with Zero Columns and Rows

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m≥nm\ge n; defaults n=45n=45, m=100m=100
Factory: linfun_r1z()

Define s(x)=∑j=2n−1jxjs(x)=\sum_{j=2}^{n-1}jx_j. The residuals are

r1(x)=−1,ri(x)=(i−1)s(x)−1,i=2,…,m−1,rm(x)=−1. \begin{aligned} r_1(x)&=-1,\\ r_i(x)&=(i-1)s(x)-1,&&i=2,\ldots,m-1,\\ r_m(x)&=-1. \end{aligned}

Edge case: For n≤2n\le2, the sum defining s(x)s(x) is empty.

Start: x(0)=(1,…,1)x^{(0)}=(1,\ldots,1)

35. Chebyquad Function

Dimensions: n≥1n\ge1, m≥nm\ge n; default n=50n=50 and m=nm=n
Factory: chebyquad()

Let Ti*(u)=Ti(2u−1)T_i^*(u)=T_i(2u-1) be the Chebyshev polynomial shifted to [0,1][0,1], with

T0*(u)=1,T1*(u)=2u−1,Ti*(u)=2(2u−1)Ti−1*(u)−Ti−2*(u). \begin{aligned} T_0^*(u)&=1,\\ T_1^*(u)&=2u-1,\\ T_i^*(u)&=2(2u-1)T_{i-1}^*(u)-T_{i-2}^*(u). \end{aligned}

For i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m,

ri(x)=1n∑j=1nTi*(xj)−ci,ci={0,i odd,−1/(i2−1),i even. r_i(x)=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^{n}T_i^*(x_j)-c_i, \qquad c_i= \begin{cases} 0,&i\text{ odd},\\ -1/(i^2-1),&i\text{ even}. \end{cases}

Calling chebyquad() derives m=nm=n from the parameter-vector length. Pass an explicit m to the factory to use an overdetermined instance with m>nm>n.

Start: xj(0)=j/(n+1)x_j^{(0)}=j/(n+1)
